items.title: Israel Gorman Interview, 1959-10-21
items.q: I never got to hear him except the records he made with Pirone

ctx.x: Well, I talk, but I studied many times. I said, well, I said, he was telling me, he said, well, he's going and then he's going to write me and tell me just how it made out, but I never did got no, no letter from this dollar.

Well, I was going to ask a little bit more about T.O., what style, since he isn't living, I never got to hear him except the records he made with Pirone, but how did he play? What was his tone like and what style did he have? Can you tell us something?

Well, Pirone, not Pirone, T.O., T.O., he fella had a really very nice tone. He had a really clarinet tone. His clarinet was on the order of, like, say, it was very little different between him and Benny Goodman. And you know Benny Goodman is a clarinet man.

items.title: Billie Pierce, De De Pierce, Israel Gorman, Joseph "Kid Twat" Butler Interview, 1963-11-20
items.q: Now when he would have a job with Piron

ctx.x: ones yeah well i played with uh manuel perez old man joey moret played with him while chris he had a band funeral band chris kelly chris kelly had a funeral band manu perez

All he'd do mostly was parade. Right off Alexander and I was the youngest kids in the band. Old man George and Rhett would play with him. The Excelsior band would play there. You see I was taking lessons with Teo. Teo was a very fine fellow with me. He did everything to help him. Now when he would have a job with Piron, and he'd be tired playing at night, and he'd have a funeral, he'd send me by me being his scholar. You understand what I mean? That's where I got band training.
You ever played with the Onward band?
